messages:
ana: Quick heads-up — dashboards showing explosion of unique values for span.attr.prompt_text and span.attr.request_id across the api-gw pool. We need a pragmatic scrub + correlation plan.

mike: Ugh. Yep. Root cause looks like we export raw prompt bodies from the front-end service before we run the prompt-hash processor. We should stop exporting the raw text at the source.

mike: Proposal: run an OTEL processor in the agent that replaces prompt_text -> prompt_hash (HMAC-SHA256 with salt), store only first 10 hex chars of hash in attributes, and add salt_version attr. No raw prompt leaves the service.

jyoti: Strong +1 for hashing at the SDK layer (avoid sending PII to collectors). My only worry: short prefix collisions for debugging. 10 hex chars ~ 40 bits, collision rate ok for dashboarding but may bite when tracing a single user across services.

keith: For request_id we need correlation to debug timeouts. We can't drop it entirely. Option: keep full request_id internally but export a salted-hash prefix too (same salt scheme). That way queries in the console can join traces via hash while raw ids stay in internal logs.

lina: From a Console/UX POV we must be explicit: show hashed ids in panels and provide a per-tenant opt-in for storing raw ids in Private deployments only. Hosted tenants should never see raw prompts or raw user IDs in UI. Also add an indicator when salt rotation occurs so historic hashes are tagged.

mike: Example pseudocode for the agent processor we discussed:
```python
def hash_attr(value, salt, prefix_len=10):
    import hmac, hashlib
    h = hmac.new(salt.encode(), value.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return h[:prefix_len]

# attach salt_version e.g. "v3" so we can rotate
```
Make sure salt comes from local KMS cache, not env var.

ana: (typo) -- ana: nit: we should also add a small entropy check before hashing prompts: if prompt_text length < 8 or contains generic scaffold tokens, set prompt_hash = "_low_entropy" so we don't create lots of trivial buckets.

jyoti: Good call. Also suggest bucketing by deterministic sketch for very long prompts: keep hash of first 256 chars only.

keith: Operational question: do we keep prompt_hash in BigQuery raw table or push only to the span index? My vote: keep hashed attr in traces export, but stream raw (if allowed) only to private on-prem sinks. For hosted, never persist raw.

lina: Retention proposals for hosted: full span payloads (with hashed attrs) retained 7 days; sampling index + aggregates 90 days; hashes available for query but raw prompt content never persisted. Add an eval pipeline that runs on sampled raw prompts (opt-in) for quality monitoring and store under separate gated workspace.

mike: For salt management: per-tenant salt (KMS-wrapped) gives better privacy isolation. When doing cross-tenant engineering queries (SRE/debug), we can only correlate within same tenant. If we need cross-tenant debugging (rare), require an audit + unwrap with KMS.

jyoti: Implementation detail: include salt_version attribute in every span and include salt_version in downstream exporters so we can map hash prefixes to salt used. Rotation strategy: keep old salts for N days (retention window) to allow lookups then retire.

keith: Edge-case: instrumentation libraries in other langs — standardize on the prefix length and HMAC algorithm in the spec so everyone produces compatible hashes. Put a conformance test in CI for instrumentation.

lina: Console UX: cluster similar prompt_hash values and display most-frequent prompt_bucket examples, never the raw prompt. Allow engineer to request raw prompt fetch only if they have Private org access + audit log entry.

mike: Quick OTEL processor config sketch (yaml):
```
processors:
  attributes/hash_prompt:
    actions:
      - key: prompt_text
        action: hash
        new_key: prompt_hash
        algorithm: hmac-sha256
        prefix_len: 10
        salt_kms_path: projects/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...
      - key: prompt_text
        action: delete
```
Exporters then only see prompt_hash + salt_version attribute.

ana: (ana) One more perf note: do hashing in native ext (Rust/Golang) for high-throughput gateways to avoid CPU overhead on hot paths. If not available, offload to a sidecar preprocessor.

sre-bot: detect-export: triggered collector restart on collector-2. Hash-processor will be hot-deployed to staging at 12:30 UTC.

mike: Rollout plan: 1) Agent + SDK change to compute prompt_hash locally (can be toggled off). 2) Collector processor to enforce deletion and set prompt_hash if missing. 3) Dashboard changes + retention policy update. 4) Private org migration path. 5) Salt rotation tooling and audit UI. Canary on non-prod, then 10% of prod traffic, monitor error rates and dashboard cardinality.

jyoti: I'll draft the OTEL processor PR and the SDK changes. Keith, can you own the salt KMS API and versioning? Lina please draft the Console copy for privacy indicators.

keith: Yep. I'll add API endpoints for salt lifecycle and rotation metadata. Will include audit events for unwrap requests.

lina: I'll draft the UX text + a short help doc. We'll surface the "hashed attr" tooltip in the trace and span tables.

ana: thanks team. Putting this in a follow-up doc. :thumbsup:
